source_text: Applied 3 Feb. No acknowledgement. Rejected 11 May, 'we decided to move forward with other candidates'. The same role went up again on 19 May with the same requirement list and a new date.

observations.text: No acknowledgement of the application at any point before the rejection.
The rejection arrived after the application had been open for over three months.
A materially similar posting reappeared eight days after the rejection.

interpretations.text: They never actually had the headcount.
The dwell time and the repost are both consistent with a requisition that outlived its funding decision, but the sequence alone does not separate that from three other mechanisms.

compatible_entities.reason: A requisition left open past its decision produces both the dwell and the refreshed repost.
A withdrawn budget closes the search without a hire and reopens it when funding returns.
A timeout disposition explains a rejection with no human read in between.
The application never demonstrably passed this gate.

unknowns: Whether the application was read by a person at any point.
Whether the reposted requisition is the same requisition or a new one.
Whether anyone was hired into the role in the interval.
prohibited_conclusions: The posting was never a real opening.
A specific hidden mechanism is proven.
The employer acted in bad faith.
